mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and suppresses corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in non-farm payrolls signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized), a monthly increase in housing starts above 0.5% signals heightened consumer confidence and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises > 0.5% and GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production over the past 3 months indicates robust manufacturing activity and corporate capacity utilization, supporting higher earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases over 3 months, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer price index and increase in retail sales signals disinflationary conditions that reduce real interest rates and boost equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL declines and RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized), a monthly increase in federal funds rate above 0.25% signals aggressive monetary tightening that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.03.
